Post-earnings drift after a guide-below-consensus reaction and continued sector de-rating argue for a slight negative tilt, but the stock is already near 9-10x trailing non-GAAP EPS with a large buyback, so I stay close to neutral: lognormal centred about $237 (slightly under spot) with monthly sigma ~11.5% (41% annual / 3.5).

bear.story: New CEO resets FY27 in December: organic net new ARR keeps falling (ex-Semrush Q3 net new ARR -3% y/y), freemium does not convert, operating margin compresses further on AI compute and marketing; organic growth slides to mid-single digits and EPS ~$26 gets 6.5-7x as the market prices ADBE as a melting ice cube.

base.story: Organic ARR growth ~8% stabilises, EPS grows ~10-12% with buybacks, multiple stays ~9x NTM; modest upside mostly from earnings and share shrink, not re-rating.

bull.story: AI-first ARR ($650M, +150%) and 100M freemium users start converting, organic growth re-accelerates to double digits, new management credibly defends margins; multiple recovers to 11-12x NTM EPS ~$28.5.

thesis_break_reason: Below the $190 52-week low and ~6.7x consensus FY27 EPS. reasoning: Skeptic lane. Hard facts from the Q3 FY26 10-Q/release: revenue $6.76B +13%, but Semrush ($1.87B, closed Apr 28 2026) contributes ~$120M/quarter, so organic revenue growth is ~10-11% and organic ARR ~9.2-9.3% (11th straight deceleration per bear newsletters/sell-side); RPO fell q/q ($22.27B to $22.16B) and grew only ~8% y/y; Q4 revenue guide was below consensus; net new ARR ex-Semrush -3% y/y and organic FY26 ARR target effectively cut ~200bp (MBI). Management turnover: CFO left in June (triggered 3 downgrades), CEO Narayen retires Dec 1, and he sold $31.3M of stock Sep 16-17 (34% of his position, stated as estate planning; weak signal given retirement). Downgrades from Mizuho ($270, April), Stifel ($200), Morgan Stanley, Evercore, Wolfe; consensus now Hold, avg PT ~$278. What the bears do NOT have: no accounting red flags (goodwill impairment only $70M; DOJ ROSCA case settled Mar 2026 with a $92M loss contingency), credit is A+/A2 with net debt ~$0.7B, FCF ~$10B/yr funds ~$9B/yr buybacks shrinking the count ~5%/yr, and the stock already trades ~8.6x FY27 consensus EPS. So the bear case is a terminal-value/growth story, largely priced; downside comes mainly from a December reset. Fair value ~$256 (9x skeptic FY28 EPS $28.5; FCF-after-SBC 9% yield). Scenario mixture (bear $180/25%, base $252/50%, bull $325/25%), each lognormal with 22-30% dispersion, gives a median ~$245-250 and fat left tail consistent with 41% realized vol; I shaved the middle slightly for the December guide risk.
